title: Finite product descent through rationalization and common coefficient fields
statement:
Fix the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

For every finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and put $\mathcal C_E(Y)=D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Assume the component restrictions are $\mathcal O_E$-linear equivalences $\mathcal C_E(X)\simeq\prod_i\mathcal C_E(X_i)$ and that their natural comparisons preserve completed tensor, coefficient units, and integral scalar extension for every inclusion $E\subset L$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

The rationalized restrictions induce equivalences
$$D^b_c(X,E)\simeq\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,E)$$
for the raw scalar localizations of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. On Hom groups these use the canonical isomorphism
$$\left(\prod_i H_i\right)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i\left(H_i\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\right),\qquad (h_i)_i\otimes a\longmapsto(h_i\otimes a)_i,$$
where $H_i$ are the integral component Hom modules. They commute with the coefficient extensions $E\subset L$ and preserve the rational tensor and unit of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

The common-stage restriction functor for [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] is also an equivalence
$$D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\simeq\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell).$$
Every finite tuple of component objects has a preimage represented over one finite coefficient field containing their fields of definition. Every finite tuple of component morphisms has a simultaneous representative and a global preimage over one common finite extension. Two global arrows have equal component classes if and only if their representatives agree globally after some common finite extension. These comparisons respect identities, composition, tensor products and coefficient units, using the canonical finite-stage scalar-extension comparisons. At field stages $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], so these equivalences also apply to the stated finite-Tor categories. No Karoubi completion is taken. The empty product is permitted.

proof.text: Fix $E$, write $R=\mathcal O_E$, and denote the assumed integral restriction equivalence by $r_E$. Define $R_E:D^b_c(X,E)\to\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,E)$ on objects by $r_E$ and on arrows by $f\otimes a\mapsto(r_{E,i}(f)\otimes a)_i$, extended additively. Each $r_{E,i}$ is $R$-linear by hypothesis, so this respects the balancing relation $(cf)\otimes a=f\otimes ca$. In the scalar localization composition is $(g\otimes b)\circ(f\otimes a)=(g\circ f)\otimes ba$ and the identity is $\mathrm{id}\otimes1$. Hence the displayed formula respects identities and composition and defines the rationalized restriction functor.

source.place: Hom formula and raw scalar-localization objects; explicit balancing and composition check

proof.text: For integral objects $K,M$, the assumed $R$-linear equivalence gives an $R$-linear bijection $h:\operatorname{Hom}(K,M)\to\prod_i H_i$, where $H_i=\operatorname{Hom}(r_{E,i}K,r_{E,i}M)$. Its inverse is linear: apply the injective linear map $h$ to the additivity and scalar identities for the inverse. Tensor $h$ and its inverse with $E$; the two composites are identities, since this holds on each pure tensor. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] with $N=E$ and the finite family $H_i$ (enumerate $I$ by $\{1,\ldots,t\}$). This gives the canonical bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(K,M)\otimes_R E\cong\prod_i(H_i\otimes_R E)$, sending $f\otimes a$ to $(r_{E,i}f\otimes a)_i$. It is exactly the Hom map of step 1. Thus $R_E$ is fully faithful and the isomorphism in the statement has the claimed formula. The tensor-product result includes $t=0$.

source.place: Hom formula; tensor-finite-product is the existing Mathlib tool TensorProduct.piLeft

proof.text: Every tuple of objects in $D^b_c(X_i,E)$ is a tuple of integral objects, because raw rationalization keeps objects unchanged. Essential surjectivity of $r_E$ supplies an integral object $K$ and component isomorphisms $r_{E,i}K\cong K_i$. Their images under rationalization remain isomorphisms: tensor each isomorphism and its inverse with $1$. Therefore $R_E$ is essentially surjective. Together with step 2, [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] gives the required equivalence over $E$. Work throughout in a common enlarged universe containing the finitely many categories, as required by that criterion.

source.place: Tag 02C3, lemma-equivalence-categories; rationalization keeps the integral object set

proof.text: Define $b^i_{L/E,K}:(j_i^*K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}j_i^*(K\otimes_E L)$ as the pullback comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] for $f=j_i$, followed by rationalization; it is the comparison $\theta^{j_i^*}_{E,L}$ used by the common-stage pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. On $u\otimes a$ its naturality square is the integral naturality square tensored with $a\in E\subset L$, so it commutes on arbitrary arrows by additivity. The identity and tower compatibilities of $b$ are those stated in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with the scalar-tower identifications of [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition]. The integral tensor and unit comparisons $\mu$ of the restrictions also rationalize: on two pure arrows the tensor comparison square is its integral square multiplied by $ab$, since $(u\otimes a)\otimes_E^L(v\otimes b)=(u\widehat\otimes^L v)\otimes ab$. Extend in both variables additively. The integral inverse comparisons rationalize to inverses, so these remain isomorphisms. By the item's hypothesis these comparisons preserve integral scalar extension: under $b$ and the tensor comparison $\theta^{\otimes}$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], $\mu$ over $\mathcal O_L$ corresponds to $\mu$ over $\mathcal O_E$ extended to $\mathcal O_L$, and likewise for units. Rationalization is a functor, so this square holds over $E\subset L$ too. This proves the coefficient, tensor and unit compatibility at each rational stage and across stages.

source.place: Rational level and algebraically closed level, using the explicit formulas in the current DAG definition

proof.text: Define common-stage restriction by $(E,K)\mapsto((E,j_i^*K))_i$. For an arrow represented by $u:K\otimes_E L\to M\otimes_F L$, its $i$th component is represented by $(b^i_{L/F,M})^{-1}\circ j_i^*(u)\circ b^i_{L/E,K}$. These source and target identifications have precisely the directions shown: $b$ takes extension of the restricted object to restriction of the extended object. If $u$ is replaced by its extension to $L'$, naturality and the tower identity of step 4 identify the two displayed arrows after extension to $L'$. Representatives equal at a further stage therefore have equal images. At a common stage the middle factors $b\,(b)^{-1}$ cancel in a composite; identity arrows give $(b)^{-1}b=1$. Hence this prescription is a well-defined functor. This uses the representative and equality rules in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the common-stage pullback formula in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

source.place: Displayed Hom colimit and common-stage composition, with the explicit current DAG pullback formula

proof.text: Any finite list of coefficient fields has a common finite upper bound: start with $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and replace the current field successively by its compositum with the next field. The nonemptiness, finiteness of a binary compositum, and its upper-bound property are stated in [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Induction on the length gives a field containing the whole list; the zero-length list uses $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Apply this construction whenever the following steps collect finitely many fields. No assertion about an infinite family is used.

source.place: Directed coefficient index; finite repetition of the binary upper-bound construction

proof.text: Given component objects $(E_i,K_i)$, choose by step 6 a finite $L$ containing all $E_i$. The pair $(E_i,K_i)$ is isomorphic to $(L,K_i\otimes_{E_i}L)$: both forward and backward arrows are represented at $L$ by the identity of $K_i\otimes_{E_i}L$, using the identity-extension identifications; their composites are identity classes. Step 3 at $L$ gives $K\in D^b_c(X,L)$ with $j_i^*K\cong K_i\otimes_{E_i}L$ for every $i$. Consequently $(L,K)$ is a preimage up to the specified component isomorphisms. This proves essential surjectivity and the asserted common-field representation of every finite tuple of objects.

source.place: Objects are finite-stage pairs; transition objects represent isomorphic common-stage objects

proof.text: Fix global objects $A=(E,K)$ and $B=(F,M)$. Each component arrow between their restrictions has a representative $v_i$ over a field $L_i\supset E,F$. Choose $L$ containing all $L_i$ and $E,F$ by step 6 and extend these arrows to $L$. Conjugate by $b^i_{L/E,K}$ and $b^i_{L/F,M}$ to regard them as arrows $j_i^*(K\otimes_E L)\to j_i^*(M\otimes_F L)$. Fullness of $R_L$, proved in step 2, supplies one global arrow $u:K\otimes_E L\to M\otimes_F L$ with exactly these component arrows. Its common-stage class maps to the given tuple by the formula in step 5. Thus restriction is full, with a simultaneous representative and global preimage over $L$. For arrows between arbitrary component tuples first use the object preimages and their component isomorphisms from step 7, conjugate the arrows by those isomorphisms, and apply this construction; finitely many additional representative fields can be included in $L$.

source.place: Hom colimit representatives and common-stage composition; finite-field arrow lifting

proof.text: Let two global arrows from $A$ to $B$ have equal component classes. Represent them at fields $L_0,L_1$ and extend both to a common $L$. For each $i$, equality of the two component classes means, by the explicit equality rule in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], equality of their representatives at some finite $M_i\supset L$. Choose one $M$ containing all $M_i$ and $L$ by step 6. Naturality of the scalar comparisons in step 4 makes the restrictions of the two global representatives equal at $M$. Faithfulness of $R_M$ from step 2 then makes the global representatives equal at $M$. Conversely global equality at a common finite extension implies all component equalities there by functoriality. This proves faithfulness and the stated if-and-only-if for eventual global equality. No transition map on Hom groups has been assumed injective.

source.place: Equality of representatives after a further common finite extension

proof.text: Steps 7--9 verify essential surjectivity and bijectivity on all Hom sets, so [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] gives the algebraically closed coefficient equivalence. For tensor compatibility, the common-stage comparison for $(E,M),(E',N)$ is the class at $F=EE'$ of $\mu_F$ composed with the inverses of the comparisons $b$ for $M$ and $N$ (step 4). To check naturality, represent the finitely many objects, input arrows and their tensor operations over one common $L$ using step 6. By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the tensor arrow at that stage is $\theta_{\mathrm{target},L}^{-1}(u\otimes_L^L v)\theta_{\mathrm{source},L}$, with $\theta$ the scalar-extension comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. The cross-stage square of step 4 turns the extension of the comparison at $F$ to $L$ into $\mu_L$ conjugated by these same $\theta$ and $b$. At $L$ naturality of $\mu_L$ (step 4) gives the required square. Naturality and tower compatibility of $\theta$ and $b$ then make the equality persist at any larger field. Hence it is an equality of common-stage classes, independent of representatives. The coefficient unit is represented at any finite field; its restriction comparison rationalizes by step 4 and is carried along extensions by the unit part of the same cross-stage square. Identities and composition were checked in step 5. The structural equations for these comparisons can each be checked over a common field and are the finite-stage equations of step 4.

source.place: Tag 02C3, lemma-equivalence-categories; common-stage tensor formulas of def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom

proof.text: If $I=\varnothing$, use $L=\mathbf Q_\ell$ for the empty tuple. The assumed integral equivalence with the terminal empty product supplies an object, and every integral Hom module is zero because its underlying set is a singleton. Its tensor product with $E$ is zero, so every rational Hom set is a singleton; the common-stage Hom colimit is again a singleton. In the argument of step 9 take $M=L$, since there are no component equality witnesses to collect, and use the rational Hom bijection of step 2 into the singleton empty product. Thus all arguments include the empty case. Finally [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] defines $D^b_{ctf}(Y,E)=D^b_c(Y,E)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)=D^b_c(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$, so the two equivalences apply to those finite-Tor categories without a further theorem. All constructions used integral objects, scalar-localized arrows and finite-stage pairs; none adjoins an idempotent summand.
